questions: Does verify_post_anchor run a linkage check, and what passes without one?
Why is the duplicate check unreachable once a ledger grows?
Is the tainted-anchor defect independent of the linkage gap or a consequence of it?
What would strengthening cost on this repository's own ledger?
Which consumers would a stricter check affect?

findings.finding: verify_post_anchor performs no linkage pass; an entry chaining from the wrong predecessor satisfies its own arithmetic and classifies ok
findings.evidence: 4-entry fixture: verify() exit 1 naming both breaks, verify_post_anchor exit 0 'post-anchor clean'

findings.finding: the duplicate check fires only when n >= boundary, and boundary is max(ok_entries), so the window is one entry
findings.evidence: same fork: exit 1 as high-water mark, exit 0 after two appends, downgraded to tolerated pre-boundary residual

findings.finding: the tainted-anchor defect is a consequence of the linkage gap, not independent: the entry classifies ok because no linkage check runs, then becomes the boundary
findings.evidence: fixture: verify() reports TAINTED Entry #4, verify_post_anchor reports OK Entry #4 and boundary=#4

findings.finding: strengthening is safe to make strict on this repository
findings.evidence: real ledger at 757 entries: 0 duplicate numbers, 0 sequence breaks, both modes exit 0

findings.finding: four consumers, two of them governance gates; ledger_upgrade validates rewritten ledgers with this function and could reject an upgrade that previously succeeded
